title: Here Comes Charlie, the live album, and why they kept a quintet
summary: Sam objects to the tired music for Here Comes Charlie, a live album with Lloyd sells poorly, and the band drops the sextet.

story.theme_name: In the studio: making records, then and now
story.community_name: Record labels, producers and the business of making albums

blocks.x: You know, uhm, like uh, one time the record company dropped a movie, I don't know, they made a movie called Here Comes Charlie. Do you remember that movie? It was a movie about a dude died and came back a woman.
Oh yeah, now I remember that one.
Uh, was it Debbie Reynolds, I think she, I think it was. It was a tired movie, man, it was really, but the music was more tired than the movie.

So they wanted, they always bringing, coming to Cannonball. "Hey".... dropped the score say we want you to record Here Comes Charlie. And that was one of the tiredest melodies you ever want to hear man, and then I just grit my teeth man, everytime we got ready to play that thing, man; it wasn't nothing man, and I also told him about that too, man. I said we shouldn't play this and uh well so...
Yeah, I told Cannon he shouldn't play the shit man. But uh, as we went on down the line, we also made a uhm, uhm, a live album and uh from Shelly Man's Hole.* Remember that club?
Made a live album from, with Charles Lloyd in the band.
And uh, that record didn't do so good either. I don't think it did so good and uhm, so when Charles left to get his band uh, they decided to keep a quintet.
You know, didn't want to have another sextet, another...
No, cause everybody, they figure all the tenor players are coming in there and staying in, and everybody get famous and they get their own band.
